zusbml

Overview

SBML, the Systems Biology Markup Language, is how models of biochemical networks, pharmacokinetics and cell signaling are shared: hundreds of them are curated in BioModels. But an SBML file describes reactions between species in compartments, and a solver wants dX/dt for each state. The translation, with amounts against concentrations, compartments that change size, conversion factors and events, is where hand-written versions go wrong. The R packages that read SBML either need the libSBML system library or are no longer maintained.

zusbml reads an SBML document into one R object, writes it back as SBML, and derives from it the equations a solver needs, with nothing but R installed.

  • Derivation is the point. sbml_odes() gives the states, their right-hand sides, the assignments and the events as R expressions; sbml_derivs() turns them into a function for deSolve, with SBML’s event semantics (delays, priorities, persistence) included.
  • Checked against the SBML Test Suite. All 1,384 cases of the SBML Test Suite 3.5.0 within the supported set reproduce their reference results under each case’s own tolerances. The other 308 Level 3 Version 2 cases use algebraic rules, delay, fast reactions or SBML packages, and are refused by name rather than approximated.
  • Pure R. The only package zusbml imports is zuxml, for the XML; there is no system library to install.
  • Round trips. Reading, writing and reading again gives an identical model, for every readable Test Suite case and fifty curated BioModels.

Installation

zusbml is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zusbml")

Usage 

library(zusbml)

The package comes with a small model of a drug taken by mouth: absorbed from the gut into the central compartment, eliminated from there, and dosed a second time at hour 12. sbml_read() takes a file, a URL or the XML itself.

m <- sbml_read(system.file("extdata", "dosing.xml", package = "zusbml"))
m
#> <sbml_model 'dosing'> SBML Level 3 Version 2
#>   compartments  2
#>   species       2
#>   parameters    3
#>   reactions     2
#>   events        1

Each kind of element is a data frame. The drug in the gut is an amount; the drug in the central compartment is a concentration.

sbml_species(m)[, c("id", "compartment", "initial_amount", "has_only_substance_units")]
#>         id compartment initial_amount has_only_substance_units
#> 1 drug_gut         gut            100                     TRUE
#> 2     drug     central              0                    FALSE

sbml_odes() derives the equations. The concentration’s right-hand side is divided by the volume of its compartment, and each reaction id stands for its rate.

eq <- sbml_odes(m)
eq$rhs
#> $drug_gut
#> -absorption
#> 
#> $drug
#> (absorption - elimination)/central
eq$assignments
#> $absorption
#> ka * drug_gut
#> 
#> $elimination
#> ke * drug * central

sbml_derivs() gives deSolve what it needs, including the event: the drug in the gut goes back up at hour 12.

f <- sbml_derivs(m)
deSolve::ode(
  attr(f, "y0"), times = c(0, 6, 12, 18, 24), func = f, parms = attr(f, "parms"),
  method = "lsodar", rootfunc = attr(f, "rootfunc"), events = attr(f, "events")
)
#>   time     drug_gut     drug
#> 1    0 1.000000e+02 0.000000
#> 2    6 2.478742e-01 3.733943
#> 3   12 1.000006e+02 1.133898
#> 4   18 2.478759e-01 4.075490
#> 5   24 6.144424e-04 1.236769

sbml_write() writes SBML Level 3 Version 2, and reading it back gives the same model. sbml_to_rxode2() writes the equations for rxode2 instead.

identical(sbml_read(sbml_write(m)), m)
#> [1] TRUE

Functions are named sbml_*(): sbml_read() and sbml_write() for documents, an accessor per element kind, and sbml_odes(), sbml_derivs() and sbml_to_rxode2() for equations.

  • The reference index documents every function.

Related work

zusbml follows the SBML Level 3 Version 2 Core specification and reads Level 2 Versions 4 and 5 by mapping them to it. It is checked against the SBML Test Suite and curated models from BioModels, neither of which it ships. libSBML is the reference implementation; zusbml does not use it.
